reason: The `'last'` path evaluates `key_fn` twice per row, which can yield incorrect deduplication when the callable has side effects or returns changing keys. Existing tests only cover a pure key function and miss this correctness issue.

The `'last'` implementation computes `key_fn` once to build last indices and again to select rows, so a stateful or otherwise non-deterministic key function can produce incorrect results; it also needlessly doubles key extraction work. Cache each row’s key during the first pass and use that cached key for selection before merging.
